blocks.title: Introduction: The `Quantum First'-Program
blocks.content:
If our world, as is widely believed, is quantum, it is in principle representable as a single vector evolving in Hilbert
space, and thus, all spatiotemporal notions must be reducible to this description. This suggests a research program
that has been variously called ‘Hilbert Space Fundamentalism’ [1], ‘Mad Dog Everettianism’ [2], ‘extreme Occam’s
razor’ [3], or simply ‘physics from scratch’ [4]. Essentially, rather than trying to find quantized versions of classical
notions, whether of spacetime or of classical fields, one instead starts with a quantum description, and aims to locate
the appr

Indeed, the links appear so deep that Susskind has proposed to generalize ER = EPR, the conjecture that quantum
entanglement is equivalent to wormholes in spacetime [6], to GR = QM, proposing that ‘where there is quantum
mechanics, there is also gravity’ [7]. Hence, a quantum system does not merely come equipped with a geometry, but

The Bloch Sphere and the Complex Hopf Fibration
Above, we have already introduced the Bloch sphere representation of single qubits. The normalization condition
|c0|2 + |c1|2 = 1 implies that the Hilbert space of a single qubit is the 3-sphere S3. However, quantum states are

THE OCTONIONIC CASE: THREE QUBITS
The third step in this construction takes us to the octonionic case. Remarkably, this is also the final step: the
octonions are the largest division algebra, and the octonionic one is the final Hopf fibration. The next algebra that
can be constructed via the Cayley-Dickson process, the sedenions, is no longer a division algebra, as it possesses
nontrivial zero divisors, and hence, the Hopf map cannot always be defined.

blocks.title: Entanglement and Massive Particles
blocks.content:
ENTANGLEMENT AND MASSIVE PARTICLES
The above has given us a way to interpret the degrees of freedom contained within a single octonionic qubit as
the left-handed part of one generation of the fermion content of the Standard Model, transforming under the gauge
symmetry SU(3) × SU(2) × U(1)/Z6 in the appropriate way, after singling out a complex direction and splitting O
into C ⊕C3.

blocks.title: Conclusion
blocks.content:
CONCLUSION
The present study draws inspiration and arguments from several disparate sources, aiming to integrate them into
a coherent whole. These avenues are, as delineated above:
◦The ‘quantum first’ program of deriving physics from scratch, starting from a quantum state in Hilbert space,
◦the Kaluza-Klein-like emergence of forces and matter from dimensional reduction,
◦the connection between spacetimes of dimensions 2 + 1, 3 + 1, 5 + 1 and 9 + 1 and the division algebras R, C,
